subject: Integration recap: tracing fields & latency headers
messages:
From: Devon Liu <devon.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff — quick recap

Thanks for the call today, Ben. Quick follow-ups from our infra side:

1) Auth — we currently run a mix of short-lived mTLS certs and an internal API gateway that issues JWTs. We want to understand the simplest auth pattern to get an end-to-end demo running (no org-level SSO yet).
2) Tracing/observability — ops asked about propagating trace ids through the Redwood calls and getting a latency breakout on each hop. They also want a stable header we can index in Splunk.
3) Embeddings / rerank — will the hosted API give us token-level cost estimates, and can we run a local reranker via your dedicated pool?

Attaching our current integration checklist. Can you send a short of the SDK steps, the auth flow you recommend for trial, and the observability fields we should add to our logs?

—Devon
Devon Liu
Platform Engineer, Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Liu <devon.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff — quick recap

Devon — thanks for the clear notes and for looping ops in. TL;DR: we can get you a working end-to-end demo in ~48 hours with the following: SDK quickstart, API-key short-lived example, and a recommended set of observability headers/fields to wire into Splunk. Details below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Auth recommendation for trial
- For the POC, we recommend scoped API keys with automatic rotation (we can surface a short-lived key via a one-time link) rather than mTLS. This minimizes infra changes while preserving isolation.
- For longer-term, we support JWTs issued by your gateway and mutual-TLS in Private deployments.

2) SDK setup & routing
- SDK quickstart: language-specific packages (Python/Node) that wrap request routing and automatic retries. See attached redwood-sdk-setup.pdf for the sample commands.
- Routing: you can pin a route to "dedicated-us-gpu" or prefer cost routing (hosted fallback -> dedicated when pinned). The SDK accepts a routingHint param.

3) Observability fields (recommended list)
- Trace propagation headers: X-Request-ID (client-generated UUID), X-Trace-ID (OpenTelemetry trace id), X-Span-ID (span id)
- Latency breakdown headers returned by Redwood: X-RW-Client-Latency, X-RW-Server-Latency, X-RW-KV-Cache-Latency, X-RW-Kernel-Latency
- Cache metadata headers: X-RW-KV-Cache-Hit (true/false), X-RW-Model-Variant
- Per-token cost header (for hosted): X-RW-Token-Cost (microunits) — note: that's per-response aggregate for now

4) Embeddings & rerank
- Hosted embeddings API supports per-request model selection. We emit embedding-dimension and model-name in response headers; cost estimates are in Token-Cost header.
- Reranking: you can run a lightweight reranker in-hosted for evaluation, but production rerankers with heavy batching should use Dedicated or Private to control latency/cost.

Next steps (proposed):
- We’ll send the SDK quickstart and a one-time API key link. (Action: Ben, today)
- Marissa to provide a short observability mapping CSV (fields -> Splunk keys) and a Grafana dashboard template. (Action: Marissa, by EOD tomorrow)
- Devon to confirm which routing mode to test: "pin-to-dedicated" or "cost-fallback". (Action: Devon, by Wed)

Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Liu <devon.liu@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff — tracing fields & latency headers

Hi Devon — following Ben's breakdown, I attached an obs-field-mapping.csv that maps Redwood headers to Splunk field names and provides sample parsers. A few operational notes: 

- Use X-Trace-ID as the primary indexed key in Splunk. We recommend sampling at 100% for 48 hours during POC, then move to 10% for production unless you need end-to-end traces for debugging.
- If you want Grafana dashboards, import the attached JSON template after you wire the headers into your extractor. Key panels: per-route p95 latency, kernel vs KV cache latency waterfall, and model-variant error rates.
- For low-latency health checks, add a short polling route that hits /v1/health and records X-RW-Server-Latency — this is much cheaper than full-token calls.

Quick example log line we recommend indexing: 
- timestamp=2027-05-11T16:00:00Z trace_id=<X-Trace-ID> span_id=<X-Span-ID> route=dedicated-us-gpu model=gpt-4o-rw latency_ms=134 kernel_ms=90 kv_cache_ms=12 cache_hit=true tokens=48 cost_microunits=123

I’ll drop the dashboard JSON in the Drive link Ben shared and can hop on a 30-min runbook session with your ops team tomorrow if you want.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

(Attachment: obs-field-mapping.csv)

From: Devon Liu <devon.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff — tracing fields & latency headers

Thanks Ben/Marissa — this is great. A couple clarifications before we kick off the POC: 

- For the POC we'll accept the scoped API key route to move quickly. Can you confirm the rotation cadence and whether the SDK will automatically refresh keys if we use a short-lived token?
- For the trace header: we emit trace_id as traceparent/W3C trace context. Can Redwood accept traceparent or do we need to map to X-Trace-ID?
- For reranking: we want to test a 2-stage flow (embedding -> candidate retrieval -> rerank). Will the hosted path add more than ~8–12ms per call relative to dedicated (we're sensitive to p99 spikes)?

If you can confirm those three points I’ll schedule the ops runbook slot for Wednesday 14:00 PT.

—Devon

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Liu <devon.liu@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff — tracing fields & latency headers

Devon — quick answers inline and we'll bring details to the runbook: 

- Key rotation: scoped API keys rotate every 24 hours for POC tokens by default; SDK will accept a refresh token endpoint. We can also surface a one-click short-lived key that expires after 12 hours. (Ben: I’ll send the one-time link now.)
- Traceparent/W3C: we accept W3C tracecontext (traceparent) natively. If you prefer X-Trace-ID we can add a header mapping in the SDK; otherwise pass traceparent and we’ll surface X-RW-Trace-ID for backward compatibility in logs.
- Rerank latency: hosted path for lightweight rerank (<= 64 tokens) typically adds 6–15ms median vs dedicated; p99 depends on traffic and batching — Dedicated gives more consistent p99. For the POC we recommend hosted with a pin-to-dedicated fallback if you see p99 spikes.

We’ll cover the SDK refresh flow and the header mapping in the runbook. See you Wednesday 14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
